question.problem:
Given that $h(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}})$ and

$$
\frac{∂h}{∂x}=\frac{1}{x},\,\frac{∂h}{∂y}=-\frac{2}{y},\,\frac{∂h}{∂z}=\frac{1}{z},
$$

find the set of values $(x,y,z)$ on which all partial derivatives of $h$ exist.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $h(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}})$ is defined only when $xz>0$ and $y\ne 0.$ So, the domain of $h$ is 

$$
{D}_{h}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,xz>0\,\text{and}\,y\ne 0\}.
$$

As for the partial derivatives, we have the following.

- The function ${h}_{x}=\frac{1}{x}$ is defined only when $x\ne 0.$ So, the domain of ${h}_{x}$ is 

$$
{D}_{{h}_{x}}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,x\ne 0\}.
$$

- The function ${h}_{y}=-\frac{2}{y}$ is defined only when $y\ne 0.$ So, the domain of ${h}_{y}$ is 

$$
{D}_{{h}_{y}}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,y\ne 0\}.
$$

- The function ${h}_{z}=\frac{1}{z}$ is defined only when $z\ne 0.$ So, the domain of ${h}_{z}$ is

$$
{D}_{{h}_{z}}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,z\ne 0\}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partials of $h$ exist on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{h}\cap {D}_{{h}_{x}}\cap {D}_{{h}_{y}}\cap {D}_{{h}_{z}} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,xz>0\,\text{and}\,y\ne 0\}\cap \{(x,y,z)\,:\,x\ne 0\} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\cap \,\{(x,y,z)\,:\,y\ne 0\}\cap \{(x,y,z)\,:\,z\ne 0\} \\  & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,xz>0\,\text{and}\,y\ne 0\}.\end{aligned}
$$
